title_original: Microdrama revenues hit $20bn in 2026, but profits remain elusive outside China
excerpt_original: A report from Media Partners Asia show a 24% rise in global revenue.

blocks.text: Global microdrama revenue has hit $20bn in 2026, rising 24% year-on-year, but the business struggles to make profit outside of China, according to a report from Media Partners Asia (MPA).

Total revenue will reach $32bn by 2031 at a growth rate of 9.8% per year, according to MPA’s second Micro-Drama Economy report. China is projected to generate $15.2bn this year, accounting for 76% of total microdrama revenues, while dedicated apps outside China earn $4.87bn.

Profit in China will likely slow to 6.7% in 2031 as viewing levels off, taking revenue there to $21bn. The MPA notes that leading players such as ByteDance, Tencent and Kuaishou do not refer to microdrama content in recent financial reporting, suggesting it might be less of a priority moving forward. The three companies collectively account for 82% of the Chinese market, with ByteDance, which operates Hongguo and Douyin, earning 56% of China’s revenues.
Advertising on free services overtook paid viewing in China in 2025. It will account for 69% of revenue there this year and it is projected this figure will increase to 79% by 2031.

MPA figures calculate revenue as what consumers and advertisers pay before dedicated app-store and payment fees. MPA’s estimates exclude producer outlays on AI models and platform investment in China. As a result, their projections are narrower than the National Radio and Television Administration’s $15bn (RMB100bn) estimate for 2025.

Outside China, earnings are significantly reduced because 56% is spent on marketing and a further 18% goes to app stores and payment providers. About one user in 12 pays in a given month, so profit margins remain thin.

Global revenue is worth $4.87bn. The highest earnings come from the US at $1.71bn, but revenue has fallen 2% year-over-year. The Asia Pacific region (excluding China) is expected to overtake this figure by 2029. MPA expects direct payments to supply about half of revenue growth outside China in 2027.

Microdrama groups DramaBox and Reelshort report revenues of more than $1bn a year, but overall earnings are considerably less. The MPA noted that DramaBox recorded a net margin of 3.2% last year while ReelShort lost $12m, although it made $8m back in the first quarter of this year.

Collectively, the four apps ReelShort, Kunlun, NetShort and DramaBox, which recently announced a merger with GoodShort, now account for 65% of revenue outside of China. Each is Chinese-owned or backed.

The fastest growth has been reported in India where revenues have tripled this year for local platforms like Kuku TV and Story TV, making it the largest Asian market outside of China, ahead of Japan and South Korea with a revenue of $322m. In Korea, local company Vigloo is competing with Chinese-backed apps, as is Fuji TV’s Fod Short in Japan, thanks to established audiences drawn in through local IP and talent.
While the microdrama business continues to evolve, MPA predicts TikTok will be key to growth outside of China, gaining “significant scale” in the US and Southeast Asia by 2031.
TikTok’s parent company ByteDance seeks to replicate the model used in China, drawing audiences in through free, advertising-funded apps before monetising later.

MPA notes that YouTube and Meta are not likely to make a larger impact on the microdrama business. Free platforms are not expected to displace the paid apps, which own the IP and the paying relationships.

New titles listed on apps released outside of China increased from around 100,000 in 2025 to 440,000 in 2026, counting series made in different languages more than once. Live-action still holds most of the top 50 titles on five of the six platforms tracked.

Some 75% were made using AI, with research showing that an AI-made title costs “about a tenth of a series filmed in Los Angeles”. In China, AI accounts for about nine out of 10 titles released in 2026, but only 20% of the year’s revenue.

The report draws on MPA’s Micro Drama Database, which tracks 50 apps in 12 markets; consumer measurement from ampd, MPA’s consumer-insights business; a title tracker covering about 35,000 titles; and company accounts and interviews across the industry.
